key_insight: The paper enables one-step, latent-free image generation by decoupling the network's output space from the loss space and training a pixel-space flow—Pixel MeanFlow (pMF)—that maps noise directly to images in a single step.
problem_solved: Modern diffusion and flow models rely on many sampling steps and/or latent spaces (encoders/decoders); pMF targets both bottlenecks to provide fast, simpler, high-quality image generation without latents or iterative sampling.
method: Formulate network output space and loss space separately so the model can predict pixel-domain mean updates while optimizing a suitable loss in a different space.
Train a flow-based model that operates directly on pixels (Pixel MeanFlow) to learn a one-step mapping from random noise to images.
Adopt objective and architectural choices to stabilize training and preserve sample quality without requiring an encoder/decoder or multi-step refinement.
impact: Delivers dramatic sampling-speed improvements and a simpler generation pipeline—helpful for practitioners needing real-time or resource-constrained image synthesis while maintaining competitive image quality.

paper_title: One-step Latent-free Image Generation with Pixel Mean Flows
paper_authors: Yiyang Lu, Susie Lu, Qiao Sun, Hanhong Zhao, Zhicheng Jiang
